sections.h2: How a Royal Oak sale works
sections.html:
Sellers here deal with the city's Assessing and Building divisions and the Oakland County Register of Deeds, and one variable is whether the house is a registered rental. An owner-occupied house needs the deed, the transfer affidavits and the tax steps, while a rental adds city registration and inspection rules.

Royal Oak lies on the Woodward Corridor roughly 10 miles north of downtown Detroit, within easy reach of I-75 and I-696. Many buyers want to be near the restaurants and nightlife around Main Street and Washington Avenue. Expect questions on noise, parking and event traffic, and answer them honestly for event weekends. Older streets have a mature tree canopy, so photograph the yard in full leaf.

Federal figures for 2020 to 2024 put the middle owner-occupied home at $328,700, with owners in 68.0 percent of homes and rent at $1,381. Household income is $101,109 at the midpoint.

Households run small, averaging 1.98 people, and 42.3 percent of 2020 households held one person. An estimated 57,583 people lived here in July 2025, 1.1 percent fewer than the 2020 base, and numbers have hovered near 57,000 to 58,000 since 2010. On 11.79 square miles that is about 4,937 people per square mile, so a listing competes with many similar blocks and presentation matters.

Royal Oak Schools teach most children, though a portion of the city's land is zoned to Berkley Public Schools, so confirm your address before listing. Families will ask about the district boundary first.

A landlord registers with the city before any tenant moves in, and the Building Division then inspects rental units under the Property Maintenance Code. The owner has to name a responsible party within 30 miles, post the address inside the unit, keep within occupancy limits, and maintain working smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and extinguishers.

Short-term rentals also need insurance and must hand guests the city's Good Neighbor Policy. A buyer will want to see the registration paperwork, and an unregistered rental is a problem to fix before closing. Penalties escalate with each violation.

Royal Oak rental ordinance penalties
ViolationPenalty
FirstCivil fine of at least $200 plus costs
SecondCivil fine of at least $350 plus costs
ThirdMisdemeanor, fine up to $500, up to 90 days in jail, or both, and registration may be revoked

Questions go to the Building Division at building@romi.gov. Registration fees pay for the inspections, so expect a charge when a buyer registers the house after closing.

Summer taxes fall due July 31 and winter taxes February 14. A postmark will not count as proof of payment. A late summer bill accrues interest of one-half of 1 percent a month from August 1, and anything unpaid on March 1 goes to the Oakland County Treasurer. Owners may split the summer bill into two halves, due July 31 and October 31.

Assessed value is set at 50 percent of true cash value, and an inflation multiplier limits taxable value until a transfer happens. Every transferred property gets a review of its deed and affidavit by the Assessor's Office, and that review lifts the cap. For a ballpark new bill, take half the purchase price as taxable value, divide by 1,000 and multiply by the millage rate.

An owner who lived in the home before May 1 of the prior year qualifies for the Principal Residence Exemption, which carries a rate about 15 mills below a non-homestead property. When you sell, rescind your own exemption, and the buyer applies on the new home.

To appeal a value, start with the March Board of Review. Clerical errors and mutual mistakes get corrected at the July and December sessions. Parcel records are free to read on BS&A Online, so look yours over before a buyer does, and note anything that is wrong.

Staff at the county look over every document before it is recorded, and one defect can cost you weeks. The first page needs a 2.5 inch top margin with half-inch margins on all other sides, and a notary has to sign off on the deed. Deeds signed before April 6, 2017 had to state the marital status of male grantors, and those signed before March 4, 2002 needed two witnesses.

  • The Sidwell Validation Unit signs off on the legal description before payment is taken.
  • The counter is open weekdays from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
  • Copies are $1 a page, and a certified copy adds $5.
  • Recording runs $30 per deed with the $4 survey surcharge included, and a warranty deed needs a $5 tax certificate from the treasurer.

Transfer tax applies to anything with consideration above $99.99, and the seller pays it under MCL 207.523. The county takes $1.10 per $1,000 and the state takes $7.50 per $1,000.

Open your parcel record on BS&A Online and verify what it says. A rental needs its registration paperwork and the latest inspection on hand. Pick a closing date that fits the tax calendar, and find out from the title company who covers the tax certificate and recording. A cash buyer can often close faster, but the county filing and the assessor's review still apply, and the buyer's taxable value resets after the transfer. Ask for the closing date and net amount in writing from every buyer you talk to.

sections.h2: When the house is a rental
sections.html:
An occupied rental can change hands, but the buyer needs to see that the house is registered and has been inspected. Hand over the registration paperwork, the last inspection record and the current lease. Then ask the Building Division what the new owner files, since an unregistered rental is something to fix before closing rather than after.

If the buyer plans to live in the house, the rental registration question matters less, but the tenant's move-out date and your notice rights still set the closing calendar. Agree on a date in writing so nobody waits on an empty house.

Once the deed is recorded, the Assessor's Office reviews it with the transfer affidavit, and the buyer's taxable value resets. You rescind your Principal Residence Exemption so you are not billed at the lower rate on a house you no longer own. If a summer bill was split, make sure the October 31 half is paid or credited at closing. Keep a copy of the recorded deed and the closing statement with your tax records.

Check the closing statement for the transfer tax lines before you sign. The seller carries the bill, and the amounts follow the shares the county prints.

faqs.q: Must a Royal Oak landlord register before selling?
faqs.a: An occupied rental should already be registered, because registration comes before renting. Give the buyer your paperwork and ask the Building Division what the new owner must file.

faqs.q: What are Royal Oak's tax due dates?
faqs.a: The summer bill is due July 31 and the winter bill February 14. You may pay summer in two halves, with the second due October 31.

faqs.q: How does the homestead exemption change after a sale?
faqs.a: A buyer claims it on the home they are buying, and it cuts the rate about 15 mills compared with non-homestead property. You rescind yours at sale.

faqs.q: What does the county charge to file a Royal Oak deed?
faqs.a: Recording is $30 per deed including the $4 survey surcharge, and the treasurer adds a $5 tax certificate for warranty deeds.

faqs.q: Does taxable value reset when I sell in Royal Oak?
faqs.a: Yes. After the Assessor's Office reviews the deed and affidavit, the cap lifts for the new owner, and the buyer's bill can come out higher than yours.
